threads.title: AI in Education Reviews
threads.query: What do recent review papers say about the role of AI in education, e-learning and academic self-regulation?

papers.title: A qualitative systematic review on AI empowered self-regulated learning in higher education
papers.abstract: This review examines how AI applications such as chatbots, adaptive feedback systems and e-textbooks support self-regulated learning in higher education. It highlights benefits for planning, performance and reflection, while stressing that AI should reinforce rather than replace learner autonomy.

papers.title: A systematic review of AI-driven intelligent tutoring systems (ITS) in K-12 education
papers.abstract: This systematic review synthesizes 28 studies on AI-driven intelligent tutoring systems in K-12 education. It reports generally positive effects on learning and performance, but also notes that gains are less pronounced when ITSs are compared with other digital tutoring approaches.

papers.title: Research Landscape of Artificial Intelligence and e-Learning: A Bibliometric Research
papers.abstract: This bibliometric study maps research trends at the intersection of artificial intelligence and e-learning between 2010 and 2021. It identifies major countries, institutions, authors and topic clusters, and outlines how AI became a central theme in online learning research.

papers.title: Students’ voices on generative AI: perceptions, benefits, and challenges in higher education
papers.abstract: This study examines how university students perceive generative AI tools such as ChatGPT in higher education. Students report benefits for personalized support, brainstorming and research assistance, while also raising concerns about accuracy, privacy, ethics and long-term effects on learning and development.

papers.title: Future research recommendations for transforming higher education with generative AI
papers.abstract: This qualitative study discusses how generative AI may reshape higher education and argues for future-ready skills, AI literacy and new forms of assessment. It emphasizes interdisciplinarity, maker-oriented learning and the need for new research on competencies and evaluation in GenAI-supported education.

papers.title: Challenges and Opportunities of Generative AI for Higher Education as Explained by ChatGPT
papers.abstract: This article examines how generative AI systems such as ChatGPT may affect higher education through both new opportunities and new risks. It highlights support for content generation and academic assistance, while also stressing concerns around integrity, plagiarism, policy design and student critical thinking.

threads.title: Healthcare AI and NLP Reviews
threads.query: What do review papers show about machine learning, multimodal AI and NLP in healthcare research and practice?

papers.title: Automated machine learning: Review of the state-of-the-art and opportunities for healthcare
papers.abstract: This review surveys the AutoML literature with a focus on healthcare applications. It finds that automated model selection and tuning can improve accessibility for non-expert users, but broader adoption still depends on workflow integration, scale and deployment readiness.

papers.title: Multimodal machine learning in precision health: A scoping review
papers.abstract: This scoping review examines how multimodal machine learning combines heterogeneous health data such as imaging, clinical records and omics. The authors conclude that multimodal approaches often improve predictive performance, but translation into real-world precision health remains limited.

papers.title: The use of natural language processing in detecting and predicting falls within the healthcare setting: a systematic review
papers.source: International Journal for Quality in Health Care
papers.abstract: This review analyzes how NLP has been used to detect, predict and stratify patient falls in healthcare settings. It shows promising performance across several tasks, while also emphasizing the need for stronger validation and clearer reporting of model design and implementation.

papers.title: A systematic review of natural language processing applied to radiology reports
papers.abstract: This systematic review evaluates recent NLP research on radiology reports. It finds rapid growth in publications, increasing use of deep learning, and strong potential for extracting structured clinical information, while also stressing the need for reproducibility, explainability and external validation.

papers.title: Large Language Models for Health Care Text Classification: Systematic Review
papers.abstract: This systematic review synthesizes recent studies that use large language models for health care text classification tasks. It discusses performance across clinical and public health use cases, while emphasizing privacy constraints, domain-specific terminology and the need for reliable evaluation.

threads.title: Research Tools, Citation Analysis and LLM-Assisted Reviews
threads.query: How are citation analysis methods and large language models being used to support scientific research workflows and evidence synthesis?

papers.title: Scientific text citation analysis using CNN features and ensemble learning model
papers.abstract: This paper studies qualitative citation analysis by modeling sentiment and importance in in-text citations. It proposes a CNN-based feature extraction pipeline with ensemble classification, arguing that citation evaluation should go beyond raw counts and include qualitative signals.

papers.title: Large language models for conducting systematic reviews: on the rise, but not yet ready for use-a scoping review
papers.abstract: This scoping review evaluates how large language models are being tested across systematic review workflows such as literature search, screening and extraction. It finds substantial interest and early utility, but concludes that these tools are still not reliable enough for unsupervised use.

papers.title: Can large language models fully automate or partially assist paper selection in systematic reviews?
papers.abstract: This study benchmarks large language models for article selection in systematic reviews and compares fully automated and semi-automated strategies. The results suggest that LLMs can assist screening effectively, but human oversight remains important for reliability and reproducibility.

papers.title: Are ChatGPT and large language models “the answer” to bringing us closer to systematic review automation?
papers.abstract: This commentary examines whether ChatGPT and related large language models can realistically support systematic review work. The authors argue that these systems show promise for assisting review tasks, but their outputs still require careful expert vetting because plausible responses can contain serious errors.

papers.title: Can large language models replace humans in systematic reviews? Evaluating GPT-4's efficacy in screening and extracting data from peer-reviewed and grey literature in multiple languages
papers.abstract: This study evaluates GPT-4 on screening and data extraction tasks across systematic review workflows and multiple literature types. It finds that large language models can approach human-level performance in some settings, but results remain unstable enough that careful supervision is still required.
